**潘建伟**（1970年3月11日—），男，[汉族](/wiki/%E6%B1%89%E6%97%8F "汉族")，[浙江](/wiki/%E6%B5%99%E6%B1%9F "浙江")[东阳](/wiki/%E4%B8%9C%E9%98%B3 "东阳")人[[3]](#cite_note-:1-3)，[中国](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%8D%8E%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E5%85%B1%E5%92%8C%E5%9B%BD "中华人民共和国")[物理学家](/wiki/%E7%89%A9%E7%90%86%E5%AD%A6%E5%AE%B6 "物理学家")，[中国科学技术大学](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E6%8A%80%E6%9C%AF%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6 "中国科学技术大学")常务副校长、教授，[中国科学院院士](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E9%99%A2%E9%99%A2%E5%A3%AB "中国科学院院士")，现任[九三学社中央](/wiki/%E4%B9%9D%E4%B8%89%E5%AD%A6%E7%A4%BE%E4%B8%AD%E5%A4%AE "九三学社中央")副主席。多年从事[量子信息](/wiki/%E9%87%8F%E5%AD%90%E4%BF%A1%E6%81%AF "量子信息")领域的研究工作，并取得了一系列开创性的研究成果[[4]](#cite_note-4)。

## 生平

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E6%BD%98%E5%BB%BA%E4%BC%9F&action=edit&section=1 "编辑章节：生平")]

潘建伟生于浙江省[东阳市](/wiki/%E4%B8%9C%E9%98%B3%E5%B8%82 "东阳市")[[3]](#cite_note-:1-3)，1987年进入[中国科学技术大学](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E6%8A%80%E6%9C%AF%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6 "中国科学技术大学")近代物理系读书，1992年毕业，获[学士](/wiki/%E5%AD%A6%E5%A3%AB "学士")学位[[3]](#cite_note-:1-3)。1995年，在该校获[硕士](/wiki/%E7%A1%95%E5%A3%AB "硕士")学位[[3]](#cite_note-:1-3)。1996年至1999年，潘赴[奥地利](/wiki/%E5%A5%A5%E5%9C%B0%E5%88%A9 "奥地利")留学，获[维也纳大学](/wiki/%E7%BB%B4%E4%B9%9F%E7%BA%B3%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6 "维也纳大学")博士学位。2005年，加入[九三学社](/wiki/%E4%B9%9D%E4%B8%89%E5%AD%A6%E7%A4%BE "九三学社")[[3]](#cite_note-:1-3)。

2013年12月，任中国科学技术大学副校长。2015年5月，任中国科学技术大学常务副校长[[5]](#cite_note-5)。

## 社会兼职

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E6%BD%98%E5%BB%BA%E4%BC%9F&action=edit&section=2 "编辑章节：社会兼职")]

2016年6月，当选[中国科学技术协会](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E6%8A%80%E6%9C%AF%E5%8D%8F%E4%BC%9A "中国科学技术协会")副主席[[6]](#cite_note-6)。

2018年1月，当选[第十三届全国政协委员](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB%E5%8D%8F%E5%95%86%E4%BC%9A%E8%AE%AE%E7%AC%AC%E5%8D%81%E4%B8%89%E5%B1%8A%E5%85%A8%E5%9B%BD%E5%A7%94%E5%91%98%E4%BC%9A%E5%A7%94%E5%91%98%E5%90%8D%E5%8D%95 "中国人民政治协商会议第十三届全国委员会委员名单")[[7]](#cite_note-7)。

2021年1月22日，第八届[欧美同学会](/wiki/%E6%AC%A7%E7%BE%8E%E5%90%8C%E5%AD%A6%E4%BC%9A "欧美同学会")（中国留学人员联谊会）第一次全国会员代表大会召开，大会选举其担任第八届理事会副会长[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11)。

## 学术贡献

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E6%BD%98%E5%BB%BA%E4%BC%9F&action=edit&section=3 "编辑章节：学术贡献")]

2007年，潘建伟在世界上首次用光量子计算机实现大数分解量子[秀尔演算法](/wiki/%E7%A7%80%E7%88%BE%E6%BC%94%E7%AE%97%E6%B3%95 "秀尔演算法")。2009年，他带领小组成功实现了世界上最远距离的量子态隐形传输（16公里）[[12]](#cite_note-12)，2012年将纪录推展到97公里[[13]](#cite_note-13)。

2012年，潘建伟团队在合肥市建成了世界上首个规模化（46个[节点](/wiki/%E8%8A%82%E7%82%B9_(%E7%94%B5%E4%BF%A1%E7%BD%91%E7%BB%9C) "节点 (电信网络)")）量子通信网络[[14]](#cite_note-14)。

2016年，潘建伟任首席科学家的[墨子号量子科学实验卫星](/wiki/%E5%A2%A8%E5%AD%90%E5%8F%B7%E9%87%8F%E5%AD%90%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E5%AE%9E%E9%AA%8C%E5%8D%AB%E6%98%9F "墨子号量子科学实验卫星")成功发射，开展世界上首次卫星和地面之间的量子通信。2019年墨子号整体实验设计获[美国科学促进会](/wiki/%E7%BE%8E%E5%9C%8B%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%B8%E4%BF%83%E9%80%B2%E6%9C%83 "美国科学促进会")评选得[克利夫兰奖](/w/index.php?title=%E7%B4%90%E7%A7%91%E5%A7%86%C2%B7%E5%85%8B%E5%88%A9%E5%A4%AB%E8%98%AD%E7%8D%8E&action=edit&redlink=1 "纽科姆·克利夫兰奖（页面不存在）")（英语：[Newcomb Cleveland Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcomb_Cleveland_Prize "en:Newcomb Cleveland Prize")），但由于[特朗普](/wiki/%E5%94%90%E7%B4%8D%C2%B7%E5%B7%9D%E6%99%AE "唐纳·川普")总统的对中政策严审中国科学家[签证](/wiki/%E7%B0%BD%E8%AD%89 "签证")，潘建伟签证未过，故由他人代表领奖，克利夫兰奖评选委员会主席杰里米表达抗议[[15]](#cite_note-15)。

2017年，潘建伟团队构建了世界首台超越早期经典计算机（[ENIAC](/wiki/%E9%9B%BB%E5%AD%90%E6%95%B8%E5%80%BC%E7%A9%8D%E5%88%86%E8%A8%88%E7%AE%97%E6%A9%9F "电子数值积分计算机")）的光量子计算原型机[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16)。

2019年，潘建伟团队实现了20光子输入60模式干涉线路的玻色取样，其输出复杂度相当于48个量子比特的希尔伯特态空间，逼近了[量子计算优越性](/wiki/%E9%87%8F%E5%AD%90%E8%AE%A1%E7%AE%97%E4%BC%98%E8%B6%8A%E6%80%A7 "量子计算优越性")[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16)。

2020年12月4日，潘建伟带领的团队成功构建76个光子的量子计算原型机“[九章](/wiki/%E4%B9%9D%E7%AB%A0_(%E9%87%8F%E5%AD%90%E8%AE%A1%E7%AE%97%E6%9C%BA) "九章 (量子计算机)")”[[17]](#cite_note-Jiu_Zhang-17)，达成[量子计算优越性](/wiki/%E9%87%8F%E5%AD%90%E8%AE%A1%E7%AE%97%E4%BC%98%E8%B6%8A%E6%80%A7 "量子计算优越性")[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16)。

## 奖项和荣誉

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E6%BD%98%E5%BB%BA%E4%BC%9F&action=edit&section=4 "编辑章节：奖项和荣誉")]

* 2011年，当选为[中国科学院院士](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E9%99%A2%E9%99%A2%E5%A3%AB "中国科学院院士")[[18]](#cite_note-18)。
* 2015年潘建伟和陆朝阳的多自由度量子传态研究获得英国物理学会2015年度十大科学突破榜首，誉为当年度世界最重大发现[[19]](#cite_note-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20)。
* 2016年1月，潘建伟领衔的“多光子纠缠及干涉度量”项目获得2015年度[国家自然科学奖](/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E5%AE%B6%E8%87%AA%E7%84%B6%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E5%A5%96 "国家自然科学奖")一等奖。
* 获评为2016年[感动中国年度人物](/wiki/%E6%84%9F%E5%8A%A8%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E5%B9%B4%E5%BA%A6%E4%BA%BA%E7%89%A9 "感动中国年度人物")。
* 2017年9月，获得2017年[未来科学大奖](/wiki/%E6%9C%AA%E6%9D%A5%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E5%A4%A7%E5%A5%96 "未来科学大奖")物质科学奖。
* 2017年[自然科学十人](/wiki/%E8%87%AA%E7%84%B6%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%B8%E5%8D%81%E4%BA%BA "自然科学十人")获奖者。
* 2018年12月，庆祝改革开放40周年大会上获得改革先锋称号，并进行了颁奖，[[21]](#cite_note-21)在此次颁奖中的称号为“量子信息研究的创新者”。
* 2024年5月16日，潘建伟当选[英国皇家学会外籍院士](/wiki/%E7%9A%87%E5%AE%B6%E5%AD%A6%E4%BC%9A%E9%99%A2%E5%A3%AB "皇家学会院士")[[22]](#cite_note-22)。
* 2024年6月20日，潘建伟被授予香港中文大学荣誉博士学位。

args.summary:
**潘建伟**（1970年3月11日出生）是一位中国物理学家，中国科学院院士，现任中国科学技术大学常务副校长、教授，以及九三学社中央副主席。他是量子通信与量子计算领域的领军人物。

**生平与教育**：出生于浙江东阳，1987年进入中国科学技术大学，1992年获学士学位，1995年获硕士学位，1996-1999年在奥地利维也纳大学攻读博士学位，师从安东·蔡林格。2013年任中科大副校长，2015年任常务副校长。

**社会兼职**：2016年当选中国科学技术协会副主席，2018年任第十三届全国政协委员，2021年当选欧美同学会第八届理事会副会长。

**主要学术贡献**：
- 2007年：首次用光量子计算机实现大数分解量子秀尔演算法
- 2009年：实现世界上最远距离（16公里）量子态隐形传输，2012年扩展到97公里
- 2012年：在合肥建成世界首个规模化（46个节点）量子通信网络
- 2016年：任首席科学家的墨子号量子科学实验卫星成功发射，实现首次卫星与地面量子通信（2019年获克利夫兰奖）
- 2017年：构建世界首台超越早期经典计算机的光量子计算原型机
- 2020年12月：成功构建76个光子量子计算机九章，达成量子计算优越性

**主要奖项与荣誉**：
- 2011年：当选中国科学院院士
- 2015年：国家自然科学一等奖（多光子纠缠及干涉度量）
- 2016年：感动中国年度人物
- 2017年：未来科学大奖物质科学奖
- 2018年：改革先锋称号（量子信息研究的创新者）
- 2024年5月：当选英国皇家学会外籍院士
- 2024年6月：获香港中文大学荣誉博士学位

This webpage is a profile page for **Pan Jianwei (潘建伟)**, a prominent Chinese experimental physicist and professor at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), located in Hefei, Anhui Province. Born in March 1970 in Dongyang, Zhejiang, he holds a Ph.D. in experimental physics and is a member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the Academy of Sciences for the Developing World, and a foreign member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences. He currently serves as the Dean of the CAS Center for Excellence in Quantum Information and Quantum Physics.

**Research Focus:** Pan Jianwei is a leading pioneer in quantum information experimental research, specializing in quantum optics, quantum information, and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics. His systematic innovations in quantum communication, quantum computing, and multi-photon entanglement manipulation have made quantum information experiments one of the fastest-growing fields in physics. A key milestone: his team's work on quantum teleportation was selected by *Nature* in 1999 as one of "21 Classic Papers in Physics of the Century," alongside Roentgen's discovery of X-rays and Einstein's theory of relativity. His research has been repeatedly recognized as major scientific events by *Nature* and *Science*.

**Awards and Honors:** Pan has received numerous prestigious awards, including the National Natural Science Award (First Class), the Future Science Prize (Materials Science Prize), the Fresnel Prize (European Physical Society), the International Quantum Communication Award, the Lamb Medal (for laser science and quantum optics), the Cleveland Prize (AAAS), the Wood Prize (OSA), the Micius Quantum Prize, and the Carl Zeiss Research Award. He has also received China's "National Innovation Pioneer" medal (2017), the "Reform Pioneer" medal (2018), and the "Most Beautiful Striver" title (2019). In 2025, he received the Tengchong Science Prize.

Explore quantum mystery, enable quantum applications!

# 中国科大成功研制113个光子的“九章二号”量子计算原型机

2021-10-26

中国科学技术大学中科院量子信息与量子科技创新研究院潘建伟、陆朝阳、刘乃乐等组成的研究团队与中科院上海微系统所、国家并行计算机工程技术研究中心合作，发展了量子光源受激放大的理论和实验方法，构建了113个光子144模式的量子计算原型机“九章二号”，并实现了相位可编程功能，完成了对用于演示“量子计算优越性”的高斯玻色取样任务的快速求解。根据现已正式发表的最优经典算法理论，“九章二号”处理高斯玻色取样的速度比目前最快的超级计算机快1024倍。这一成果再次刷新了国际上光量子操纵的技术水平，进一步提供了量子计算加速的实验证据。相关论文于2021年10月26日以“编辑推荐”的形式发表在国际知名学术期刊《物理评论快报》上。著名量子物理学家、加拿大Calgary大学教授Barry Sanders同时受邀在Physics网站上誊写长篇评述文章，称赞该工作是“令人激动的实验杰作”（dramatic tour de force.....），“令人印象深刻的最前沿的进步”（an impressive advance over the state-of-the-art）。

                                                       图1：九章二号整体装置图(制图：陆朝阳，彭礼超)

        量子计算机在原理上可通过特定算法在一些具有重大社会和经济价值的问题方面，获得比经典计算机更强的算力。早在1981年，费曼就提出了量子计算的初步想法。大规模量子计算机的物理实现是世界科技前沿的重大挑战之一。对于研制容错的通用量子计算，因其苛刻的容错阈值和大规模的量子比特数目，离目前人类的科技发展水平尚有不小的差距。

        因此，实现对于量子计算的物理实现，国际学术界采取三步走的路线图。其中，第一个里程碑，在学术上被称为“量子计算优越性”，其含义是通过高精度地操纵近百个物理比特，用来高效地解决超级计算机都无法在合理时间内解决的特定的高复杂度数学问题，从实验上确凿地证明四十年前费曼所提出来地量子计算加速设想，并挑战“扩展的丘奇—图灵论题”。

                                  图2：九章二号144模式干涉仪（部分）实验照片(摄影：马潇汉，杨建瑞，李丰，邓宇皓)

        基于光子的玻色取样和基于超导比特的随机线路取样是实验展示量子计算优越性的两个重要方案。潘建伟团队一直在光量子信息处理方面处于国际领先水平。2017年，该团队构建了世界首台超越早期经典计算机的光量子计算原型机。2019年，团队进一步研制了确定性偏振、高纯度、高全同性和高效率的国际最高性能单光子源，实现了20光子输入60模式干涉线路的玻色取样，输出希尔伯特态空间维度达到1014，逼近了“量子计算优越性”。

        2020年，潘建伟团队成功构建了76个光子100个模式的高斯玻色取样量子计算原型机“九章”，输出量子态空间规模达到了1030，处理高斯玻色取样的速度比超级计算机快一百万亿倍，同时克服了谷歌基于“悬铃木”超导处理器的随机线路取样实验中量子优越性依赖于样本数量的漏洞。“九章”实验完成后，在理论提出玻色取样算法和证明计算复杂度的Scott Aaronson教授随后获得了由国际计算机协会颁发的ACM Prize in Computing。

        2021年，团队在“九章”的基础上，进行了一系列概念和技术创新。受到激光—“受激辐射光放大”概念的启发，研究人员设计并实现了受激双模量子压缩光源，显著提高了量子光源的产率、品质和收集效率。其次，通过三维集成和收集光路的紧凑设计，多光子量子干涉线路增加到了144维度。由此，“九章二号”探测到的光子数增加到了113个，输出态空间维度达到了1043。进一步，通过动态调节压缩光的相位，研究人员实现了对高斯玻色取样矩阵的重新配置，演示了“九章二号”可用于求解不同参数数学问题的编程能力。根据目前已正式发表的最优化经典算法，“九章二号”在高斯玻色取样这个问题上的处理速度比最快的超级计算机快亿亿亿倍。

                               图3：论文数据图。a图表示输出态空间的维度。b图表示光量子计算原型机相比超算的优势倍数。

        研究人员希望这个工作能够继续激发更多的经典算法模拟方面的工作，也预计将来会有提升的空间。量子优越性研究并不是一个一蹴而就的工作，而是更快的经典算法和不断提升的量子计算硬件之间的竞争，但最终量子并行性会产生经典计算机无法企及的算力。

        该论文第一作者是博士研究生钟翰森、邓宇皓、覃俭。上述项目受到了安徽省、上海市、科技部、中科院和基金委的支持。

On October 26, 2021, a research team led by Pan Jianwei, Lu Chaoyang, and Liu Naile from the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), in collaboration with the Shanghai Institute of Microsystems and the National Parallel Computer Engineering Technology Research Center, successfully developed "Jiuzhang 2.0," a quantum computing prototype operating with 113 photons and 144 modes. The system features phase-programmable functionality and solves the Gaussian boson sampling task — used to demonstrate "quantum computational advantage" — at a speed 10^24 times faster than the fastest supercomputers using the best classical algorithms. The work was published in Physical Review Letters as an Editors' Suggestion and praised by quantum physicist Barry Sanders of the University of Calgary as a "dramatic tour de force" and "an impressive advance over the state-of-the-art."

Key innovations in Jiuzhang 2.0 include: (1) stimulated dual-mode quantum squeezed light sources, inspired by laser technology, which significantly improved photon yield, quality, and collection efficiency; (2) 3D integration and compact optical design expanding the multi-photon quantum interference circuit to 144 dimensions; (3) dynamic phase adjustment enabling reconfigurable Gaussian boson sampling matrices, demonstrating programmability. The output state space dimension reached 10^43. This work builds on the original Jiuzhang (2020), which used 76 photons and 100 modes and achieved a speed advantage of 10^14 times over supercomputers. The team notes that quantum advantage research is an ongoing competition between classical algorithms and quantum hardware, with long-term quantum parallelism expected to eventually surpass classical capabilities.

# 潘建伟正式回归：他带回一个世界一流的科研团队

[Search all author publications](/cam/search?query=)

Vol. 6, No. 16 (2009) · 页码 7-7文章类型： **Articles**

摘要

## 摘要

今天（7月21日，下同）下午，中国科学技术大学又多了一个中心——量子工程中心。中心人不多，18个人；年龄不大，最大的1969年生人。可是他们以往的成就斐然：在世界上首次实现五光子纠缠和终端开放的量子隐形传态，首次实现复合系统量子隐形传态，首次实现六光子纠缠，首次用光子比特实验演示质因子分解……   
    
这个中心的带头人叫潘建伟，今年39岁。国际学术界对该中心的人员有个更简单的称呼：潘建伟小组。   
    
就在今天上午，一场为期两天半的名为“量子基础和技术国际研讨会：前沿和展望”正式结束，来自全世界各地的270多名量子信息和量子物理领域的学者一起见证了潘建伟小组的正式回归。   
    
以后，他们都有一个共同的称呼：中国科学技术大学教师。   
    
此前，潘建伟小组常年在中国科学技术大学和德国海德堡大学间来回奔波，兼具双重身份。对此，学界相关争议不少。   
    
潘建伟从不争辩，他只有一句话：“我是要回来的，你们会看清楚的，不需要解释。”   
    
搞科研就如做好菜，要有各种好原料   
    
潘建伟喜欢做菜。有一手好厨艺的他经常说，做一盘好菜，要有各种各样的好原料。   
    
在他看来，搞科研也是如此。从事量子信息研究就像炒菜，要有各种好的原料：有电子学的人，理论做的好的人，有控制激光的人……   
    
1999年潘建伟在维也纳大学博士毕业时，就已经取得了不俗的成就：1998年其成果被美国《科学》杂志评为年度国际十大科技新闻，1999年其论文与爱因斯坦等世界著名科学家的论文一道入选《自然》杂志的物理学百年经典。   
    
受母校中国科学技术大学邀请回国的潘建伟，在中国科大负责组建了量子物理和量子信息实验室。当时高校科研经费普遍紧张，潘建伟申请的200万元科研经费不是小数，而中科院基础科学局拨了400万元。在各方的大力支持下，设备人员都到位了，潘建伟的实验室迅速开张。   
    
但这时，潘建伟“缺位”了。在他看来，这盘菜还没到做好的时候：当时，量子纠缠最先进的技术在奥地利。尽管潘建伟在该领域已取得一定成就，但是量子纠缠技术还不够强。   
    
他向中国科技大学申请做“候鸟”：一方面在奥地利学习这项技术，一方面兼顾国内的实验室。   
    
母校同意了。到了2003年，潘建伟在量子纠缠技术方面不需要再向任何国外专家请教。但此时量子存储成为量子信息领域的前沿，而这方面力量最强的是位于德国的海德堡大学。潘建伟又向母校发出申请：接受海德堡大学客座教授的聘书，在这里继续学习。   
    
  学校再次同意了他的“候鸟”状态。   
    
潘建伟深知，量子信息集多学科为一体，要想突破，必须融合不同的学科背景。他开始为炒好这道“菜”寻找各种“好材料”。   
    
  陈帅第一次见到潘建伟是在2003年5月。当时正在北大读博士的他到德国海德堡大学做交换学生。陈帅在国内的研究方向是冷原子物理，他的指导老师正是国际冷原子物理方面的权威——施米马尔教授。施米马尔建议陈帅去奥地利参加一个学术会议，并顺便找潘建伟谈谈合作的可行性。   
    
就这样，陈帅认识了潘建伟。两人谈得很投机，潘建伟欣赏陈帅的动手能力，当场对陈帅发出邀请：你快点毕业，毕业了我们一块做。   
    
  陈帅回到北大继续自己的博士课题。2004年年底，正在进行博士论文答辩的陈帅突然接到潘建伟的邮件：找到博士后位置了吗？到我这里来吧。2005年，陈帅拎着简单的行李，来到海德堡大学，加入潘建伟小组，从事量子存储的研究。   
    
  陈凯本科和硕士学的是理论物理，博士学的是量子信息与计算，在加拿大做博士后，跟随量子通信最优秀的专家学习。当选洪堡学者后，陈凯应邀来到洪堡基金会的总部波恩访问。一次，基金会请科学家们去听音乐会，陈凯在家带孩子，夫人独自前往，碰到一个中国人，很开心地在一起聊天。一问姓名，对方正是潘建伟。   
    
尽管不从事科学研究，但陈凯的夫人经常听陈凯说起潘建伟，当场就邀请潘建伟到家中做客。于是，做量子通信的陈凯成了潘建伟小组中的一员。   
    
邓友金是“毁约”来到了潘建伟小组的。2005年，还在荷兰戴尔福特科技大学材料系做博士后的他，在海德堡大学访问时，对量子信息产生了浓厚的兴趣。他找到还在海德堡大学的潘建伟交流，潘建伟一听邓友金的学术背景，立刻来了兴趣：物理专业的本科生，理论物理学的硕士生，博士学的是统计物理。统计物理学科视野宽广，正好是这个小组欠缺的一个“角落”。   
    
邓友金当时已经答应到纽约大学做博士后研究。潘建伟向他发出两年后有机会再见的邀请。2007年4月邓友金提前结束与纽约大学的合同，来到海德堡大学潘建伟小组，与陈帅搭档做量子存储。   
    
潘建伟还刻意培养了一批“好原料”：把国内实验室一批有科研潜力的学生招到国外一流大学读博士或者从事博士后的研究，他们中很多人都换了专业，换了思维。  
  
“海德堡大学原子学科科研力量非常强，我们在海德堡是借势。每个人都要经过一段修炼。我们不断地派人去学习，团队和研究领域不断扩张，不断在科学上占领制高点。但是我们也知道，一定要重点布局，不可能面面俱到。”陈凯说。   
  
就这样，潘建伟“做菜”所需的“好原料”慢慢齐备了。   
    
在这个领域做得好，如何占领下一个制高点   
    
2003年，量子信息研究的最高端领地是量子纠缠，量子存储的研究刚刚萌芽，很多人认为这很难操控。当时大家大多用操作光子来做量子信息的处理，但是光子不能存储，总是飞来飞去的。其中一个重要问题就是产生纠缠光子的手段是不确定的，这导致长距离通信与大规模光子处理中的资源消耗太大。如果能够在光子纠缠产生之后先加以存储，到用时再处理，就会非常有效地节省资源。   
    
当时，量子存储做得最好的是哈佛大学、加州理工学院、佐治亚理工学院和麻省理工学院。在去海德堡大学之前，潘建伟小组没有做量子存储这一块的人员。   
    
这一年，潘建伟来到海德堡大学，与施米马尔教授合作从事量子存储的研究。   
    
2004年下半年，从事量子存储研究的“好原料”逐渐到位：奥赛冠军陈宇翱来了。2005年年初，陈帅到位。他们开始订购仪器，搭实验平台。1年后，做原子物理分子的苑震生从中国科大到了海德堡大学，再加上一个中国科大的学生赵博和一个德国学生，量子存储的框架搭起来了。   
    
2005年，量子存储成了量子信息领域的大热门。未雨绸缪的潘建伟则领着这帮年轻人开始做量子存储的实验了。第一年做实验，碰到不少问题：看别人的文章很明白，但是真正动手有很多细小问题。   
    
陈帅是实验能手，感触最深：用光去激发原子，让原子发出单光子，再把单光子捞出来，形同于大海捞针。这就等于10亿个单光子中，只有一个是有存储信息的。每个滤波的器件，都要精密的调节。不同的波段有不同的功能，每级做不同的功能。他们单是为了实现这个高品质的滤波就用了半年。   
    
中间难免有灰心丧气的时候。每当这时，潘建伟就现身说法：做科学是有趣的事情。不是第一个做出来，也不用很失落。做不成，就再来一次。关键是享受这个过程带来的乐趣。   
    
大约一年半时间，潘建伟小组在量子存储方面没有任何建树。组员们也不着急，就在实验上慢慢探索。2006年4月初，几乎所有的问题都碰到了，所有的问题都解决一遍了，可还是不见成果。4月底，他们绝处逢生：看到了第一个实验信号，第一套系统运行成功。小组马上决定升级打造第二套，第二套系统只用了半年。   
    
2007年小组接连做了4个实验，其中两篇上了《物理评论快报》，一篇上了《自然物理学》，还有一篇上了2008年8月的《自然》杂志。   
    
2008年，潘建伟可以很自豪地说，自己的小组是全世界做量子存储最好的小组之一了。   
    
潘建伟并不满足，他经常对小组成员说：“你在这个领域做得好，未来呢？如何占领下一个制高点？怎么能保持领先地位？”   
    
潘建伟经常很快地决断一个新工作领域，例如去开个会，听到一个新想法，发现这个东西能做后，在别人还没有反应时，潘建伟小组已经做完了。   
    
国外的冷原子技术掌握了，我们回家   
    
来自奥地利维也纳大学的物理学家Caslav Brukner这样评价潘建伟小组：“在发展量子技术方面，潘建伟小组是世界上处于领先地位的小组之一。”   
    
这绝非虚谈，潘建伟小组在国际量子信息领域成绩斐然：是国际上首次把绝对安全通信距离突破到超过百公里的3个研究小组之一，是国际上报道绝对安全的实用化量子通信网络实验研究的两个小组之一，是国际上在实用化量子通信方面开展全面、系统性实验究的两个小组之一，是在量子存储和量子中继器技术方面处于领先地位的4个国际小组之一。   
    
从组建实验室到现在，潘建伟小组已在《自然》、《自然物理》、《国家科学院院刊（美国）》、《物理评论快报》等国际一流杂志发表论文40余篇。“国外的冷原子技术我们已经掌握了。”潘建伟说。他把当初在招聘这批“好材料”时说的话又说了一遍：“我们回家吧。”   
    
很多人奇怪，海德堡大学无论从学术氛围还是实验环境，都属世界一流，为什么要回到地处合肥的中国科技大学？英国著名科学杂志《新科学家》这样评价合肥：“作为距离像上海这样的技术之都几个小时车程的安静的华东城市，合肥以其传统的豆腐和芝麻饼著称，而不是前沿物理。”   
    
早在潘建伟还在中国科大读书的时候，中科院院士朱清时就受命担任中国科大校长，他把家和实验室都搬到了学校，当时潘建伟充当了搬运工的角色。朱校长这个爱校举动对潘建伟触动很大：校长把家搬回来，把实验室搬回来，科大有希望了！   
    
回家的工作很繁琐：潘建伟小组在海德堡大学有4个实验室，一一做统计。搬家的清单，足足列了20页，大到激光器，小到12毫米的镜片也要搬回来。   
    
潘建伟的团队很优秀：每个人单独出去，有不少地方都想要。陈帅在海德堡大学做博士后期间，就有几所海外大学发出了邀请。   
    
陈凯是小组中最早回来的。在加拿大多伦多时，他遇见的很多中国人都移民了，但是他不感兴趣。“现在国内的科研条件也不错。而且，科学在优秀团队会进步更快，走到世界前沿。在这个团队是我最好的选择。”   
    
陈帅对现在的工作很满足。他与邓友金合作，一个有技术，一个有理论。“我们的成长有交叉点。如果是一个人，很难做好，但合作就会容易很多。”陈帅说，“在量子信息领域作出贡献，操控量子时间看到宏观世界现象。还有什么比这更让人激动的工作吗？”   
    
在科学的道路上，潘建伟年轻的同事们正处于事业的快速发展期。潘建伟对他们说：“你们回来后，要继承科大的传统。但是你们不能永远作为助手，一定要成长起来，独当一面。”   
    
2001年，潘建伟没有完全回到祖国工作。2009年，他带回了一个一流的科研团队。在评论完合肥留给人们的传统印象后，《新科学家》这样评价潘建伟小组：“潘和他的同事改变了这些，使得中国科学技术大学——因而也是整个中国——牢牢地在量子计算的世界地图上占据了一席之地。”

This article from CAM-Net Digest (Vol. 6, No. 16, 2009) reports on physicist Pan Jianwei's (潘建伟) formal return to China with his world-class quantum research team to join the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC). 

The 39-year-old Pan announced the establishment of a Quantum Engineering Center at USTC on July 21, 2009. His 18-member team had achieved significant breakthroughs including: first-ever five-photon entanglement, terminal-open quantum teleportation, six-photon entanglement, and experimental demonstration of prime factorization using photon bits.

Pan had been operating as a "migratory bird" between USTC and the University of Heidelberg in Germany for years, learning advanced quantum technologies. His strategy was to gather talent with diverse academic backgrounds (cold atom physics, theoretical physics, quantum communication, statistical physics) from around the world, building a comprehensive team. Key members included Chen Shuai, Chen Kai, Deng Youjin, and Chen Yuao.

The team became a world leader in quantum storage, quantum communication, and quantum relay technology. They published over 40 papers in top journals including Nature, Nature Physics, PNAS, and Physical Review Letters. The New Scientist magazine noted that Pan and his team put USTC—and by extension, China—firmly on the world map of quantum computing.

The Quantum Physics and Quantum Information Research Division (量子物理与量子信息研究部) at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) was established in 2001, led by Academician Pan Jianwei (潘建伟). The research division focuses on quantum optics and quantum information, including fundamental tests of quantum mechanics, fiber-optic quantum communication, free-space quantum communication, quantum memory and quantum repeaters, optical quantum computing, superconducting quantum computing, ultracold atom quantum simulation, quantum precision measurement, and related theoretical research. The division has built numerous experimental platforms with internationally advanced research conditions.

**Key recent news highlights:**
- "Zuchongzhi 3" (祖冲之三号) was selected as one of the 2025 China's Top 10 Scientific and Technological Advances.
- USTC successfully developed "Jiuzhang 4" (九章四号) quantum computing prototype.
- Pan Jianwei received the 2025 Tengchong Science Prize.
- Peng Chengzhi was elected as an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
- USTC achieved major breakthroughs in scalable quantum repeaters and loophole-free Hardy's paradox tests.

**Recent research progress includes:**
- Long-baseline optical interferometer based on quantum memory.
- Optical clock with stability and uncertainty reaching 10^-19 level.
- Key milestone in quantum error correction.
- Observation of "string breaking" in quantum simulation experiments.
- Detection of high-order non-equilibrium topological phases using superconducting quantum processors.

数学中心刘子文团队合作通过量子催化突破量子资源提纯极限

![](../../new/image/btn44_1.png)
![](../../new/image/btn44_2.png)
![](../../new/image/qq_xtb.png)
![](../../new/image/qq_kj_xtb.png)

**清华新闻网5月11日电** 近日，清华大学丘成桐数学科学中心助理教授刘子文与香港中文大学（深圳）数据科学学院助理教授方堃合作，在量子信息与计算理论研究中取得重要进展。研究团队提出一种基于量子催化（quantum catalysis）的、普适的、用于各类型量子资源的新型量子蒸馏方案，首次实现“一次性”（one-shot）场景中的常数开销量子蒸馏，突破了长期存在的理论极限，研究成果有望显著提升容错量子计算的效率。

量子资源蒸馏是量子计算与信息处理中的核心问题，其目标是将大量受噪声影响的低质量量子资源转化为少量高质量资源，以支撑可靠的量子信息处理。作为典型例子，魔态（magic state）蒸馏是当前容错量子计算设想中的关键瓶颈，其资源消耗决定未来大规模量子计算机的实现成本。已有理论研究表明，在实际的一次性有限资源场景中，蒸馏开销至少随目标精度按对数规律增长，即存在不可突破的“对数下界”。近年来，学界在该方向取得一系列重要进展，在平均意义下实现了低开销量子蒸馏，但相关协议往往以极大规模的批量处理为代价；随着目标精度提高，所需系统规模迅速发散，使其在实际中缺乏可实施性。如何同时实现“低开销”与“小批量”的一次性量子蒸馏是量子信息领域重要的开放问题。

针对这一问题，研究团队引入“量子催化”机制，即引入一个辅助量子系统参与量子变换，并在变换结束后保持自身不变，因此能够被重复使用。研究团队设计催化方案并证明任意多shot（multishot）量子蒸馏协议都可以在保持目标误差与成功概率不变的情况下被转化为一次性催化蒸馏协议，从而突破上述蒸馏开销的理论极限，并实现一次性常数级资源开销。尤其对于魔态蒸馏，该方法能够用有限输入开销实现任意精度的有限输出蒸馏，从而突破先前所有方案的“批量化问题”。例如，一个原本需要大规模输入与输出的协议，可以被压缩为仅产生单个输出态的一次性协议，而仍然保持相同的资源效率。这意味着容错量子计算中最昂贵的非Clifford（non-Clifford）门实际实现成本有望被大幅降低。

在理论上，该工作首次系统建立了一次性蒸馏、多次平均蒸馏与催化蒸馏之间的统一关系，证明催化蒸馏能够达到与理想多次蒸馏相同的效率。同时，研究团队提出基于催化的时空资源转换（catalytic spacetime conversion）机制，实现量子空间资源与时间资源之间的可调节交换：通过增加实验重复次数，可以进一步减少量子比特规模与资源开销，通过牺牲部分成功概率，甚至可以将蒸馏开销压缩至理论极限“1”。

![20260510-论文-刘子文-数学中心.png](/__local/9/E7/82/84DD902189B7E7874213CDFFC03_1F6ABA2A_BC4D.png)

![20260510-论文-刘子文-数学中心.png](/__local/9/E7/82/84DD902189B7E7874213CDFFC03_1F6ABA2A_BC4D.png)

图1.一次性蒸馏和多次蒸馏

![20260510-论文图例-刘子文-数学中心.png](/__local/7/CC/02/DCDC5152B01158D5E6137F96BD0_807B1C56_578A2.png)

![20260510-论文图例-刘子文-数学中心.png](/__local/7/CC/02/DCDC5152B01158D5E6137F96BD0_807B1C56_578A2.png)

图2.量子催化蒸馏：突破一次性蒸馏开销的多种理论极限

除量子态蒸馏外，研究团队还将催化理论推广至量子信道（quantum channels）变换问题，证明“信道互信息（channel mutual information）”能够完全决定量子信道之间的催化可转换性，从而解决了此前国际同行提出的一个公开猜想。

研究成果以“单次蒸馏在催化剂作用下以恒定开销进行”（One-shot distillation with constant overhead using catalysts）为题，于5月4日发表于《自然·通讯》（*Nature Communications*）。

研究工作不仅从理论上突破了量子资源蒸馏中的长期限制，也为未来容错量子计算架构设计提供了新的技术路线。此外，由于该方案主要依赖经典控制与系统重排等相对简单的操作，有望在当前快速发展的可重构原子阵列等量子硬件平台上进行实验。

**Title:** 数学中心刘子文团队合作通过量子催化突破量子资源提纯极限

**Date:** 2026年5月11日

**Source:** 清华新闻网

**Summary:**

清华大学丘成桐数学科学中心助理教授刘子文与香港中文大学（深圳）数据科学学院助理教授方堃合作，在量子信息与计算理论研究中取得重要突破。研究团队提出了一种基于量子催化（quantum catalysis）的新型量子蒸馏方案，首次在"一次性"（one-shot）场景中实现了常数开销量子蒸馏，突破了长期以来被认为是不可突破的"对数下界"理论极限。

**核心问题：** 量子资源蒸馏是量子计算中的核心问题，旨在将受噪声影响的低质量量子资源转化为高质量资源。魔态（magic state）蒸馏是容错量子计算的关键瓶颈，其资源消耗直接影响未来大规模量子计算机的实现成本。此前，一次性有限资源场景中的蒸馏开销至少随目标精度按对数规律增长。

**主要创新：**
1. 引入"量子催化"机制——一个辅助量子系统参与变换后保持自身不变，可被重复使用。
2. 证明任意多shot量子蒸馏协议可被转化为一次性催化蒸馏协议，实现一次性常数级资源开销，突破对数下界。
3. 对于魔态蒸馏，该方法能用有限输入开销实现任意精度的有限输出蒸馏，突破此前所有方案的"批量化问题"。
4. 提出基于催化的时空资源转换（catalytic spacetime conversion）机制，实现量子空间资源与时间资源之间的可调节交换。

**额外成果：** 研究团队还将催化理论推广至量子信道（quantum channels）变换问题，证明"信道互信息"能完全决定量子信道之间的催化可转换性，解决了此前国际同行提出的一个公开猜想。

**发表信息：** 研究成果以"One-shot distillation with constant overhead using catalysts"为题，于2026年5月4日发表于《自然·通讯》（*Nature Communications*）。刘子文和方堃为共同通讯作者。

**意义：** 该工作理论上突破了量子资源蒸馏中的长期限制，为未来容错量子计算架构设计提供了新路线。由于方案主要依赖经典控制与系统重排等相对简单的操作，有望在可重构原子阵列等量子硬件平台上进行实验验证。

[](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B8%85%E5%8D%8E%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6%E9%87%8F%E5%AD%90%E4%BF%A1%E6%81%AF%E4%B8%AD%E5%BF%83/7890011)

量子信息是计算机、信息科学与量子物理相结合而产生的新兴交叉学科，将为人类提供后摩尔时代的技术，为二十一世纪信息科学的发展提供新的原理和方法。量子信息技术已成为世界各国战略竞争的焦点之一。量子信息科学是量子调控的核心内容，并与信息网络、纳米等研究领域有大量的交叉，是未来中国科技发展的重大方向之一。

## 简介

播报

编辑

清华大学量子信息中心 [1]，简称量子中心，挂靠交叉信息研究院，成立于2011年1月6日，于2011年1月15日在清华大学信息科学技术大楼多功能厅举行揭牌仪式。清华大学量子信息中心由世界著名计算机学家、2000年计算机科学最高奖图灵奖得主、美国科学院院士、美国科学与艺术学院院士、中国科学院外籍院士姚期智先生领导，目标为建设世界一流的量子信息研究中心和人才培养基地，为中国量子信息的发展提供一个国际一流的研究教学平台。

## 突出贡献人物

播报

编辑

[姚期智](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%A7%9A%E6%9C%9F%E6%99%BA/0?fromModule=lemma_inlink)先生是最早进入量子信息领域进行研究的极少数计算机学家之一，为此领域作出了开创性的贡献。姚先生的研究方向包括计算理论及其在密码学和量子计算中的应用，2000年，对计算理论包括伪随机数生成，密码学与通信复杂度的突出贡献使姚期智教授荣膺图灵奖（A.M. Turing Award），成为迄今为止获得此项殊荣的唯一亚裔计算机科学家，该研究成果不仅丰富了计算机复杂理论研究领域，并对于量子信息的发展起了关键性的作用。他是研究网络通讯复杂性理论的国际前驱，于1993年最先提出量子通信复杂性，奠定了量子计算机的理论基础。1995年姚先生提出分布式量子计算模式，后来成为分布式量子算法和量子通讯协议安全性的基础。密西根大学教授、清华大学姚期智讲座教授段路明负责组建量子信息的物理实现团队，段路明教授是量子信息物理实现方面国际年轻的领军者之一，他在量子网络、量子计算机、长程量子通讯以及量子仿真物理实现方面的研究在量子信息领域有广泛而深入的影响。

## 研究方向

args.summary:
清华大学量子信息中心（简称量子中心）是清华大学下设机构，挂靠交叉信息研究院，成立于2011年1月6日，揭牌仪式于2011年1月15日在清华大学信息科学技术大楼举行。该中心由世界著名计算机学家、图灵奖得主、美国科学院院士、美国科学与艺术学院院士、中国科学院外籍院士姚期智先生领导，目标为建设世界一流的量子信息研究中心和人才培养基地，为中国量子信息发展提供国际一流的研究教学平台。

量子信息是计算机、信息科学与量子物理相结合的新兴交叉学科，是后摩尔时代技术的关键方向，也是世界各国战略竞争的焦点之一。

**突出贡献人物：** 姚期智先生是最早进入量子信息领域研究的计算机学家之一，2000年因对计算理论（包括伪随机数生成、密码学与通信复杂度）的突出贡献荣获图灵奖，是迄今唯一获此殊荣的亚裔计算机科学家。他于1993年最先提出量子通信复杂性，奠定了量子计算机理论基础；1995年提出分布式量子计算模式。密西根大学教授、清华大学姚期智讲座教授段路明负责组建量子信息的物理实现团队，是量子信息物理实现方面的国际领军者。

**研究方向：** 包括全量子网络、量子计算、量子仿真、量子算法、量子通讯复杂性理论、量子运筹学等，未来将不断扩展到其他与量子技术和信息安全相关的领域。

#### 量子中心

#### 中心介绍

量子信息是一门新兴的交叉学科领域，涉及计算机科学、信息科学和量子物理，为后摩尔时代提供了新的技术路径，探索了21世纪信息科学发展的新基础与新方法。量子信息技术已成为各国战略竞争的焦点之一。量子信息科学作为量子调控的核心，是信息网络与纳米科学等领域的交叉方向，代表了中国未来科技发展的重要战略方向之一。

清华大学于2011年1月6日正式成立量子信息中心 （Center for Quantum Information, CQI），并于2011年1月15日在清华大学FIT楼报告厅举行了揭牌仪式。该中心由2000年图灵奖得主、世界顶尖计算机科学家姚期智教授领导，旨在建设一个世界级的量子信息教学与科研平台。

姚教授是最早在量子信息领域做出开创性贡献的计算机科学家之一。他的研究兴趣主要集中在计算理论及其在密码学和量子计算中的应用。姚教授因其在计算理论方面的基础性贡献，包括伪随机数生成的复杂性理论、密码学以及通信复杂性等方面的成果，荣获2000年A.M. 图灵奖。他是图灵奖设立以来首位获此殊荣的亚洲学者，其研究成果推动了复杂性理论的发展，并对量子信息科学的进步起到了关键作用。作为网络通信复杂性理论的先驱，姚教授在1993年首次提出了量子通信复杂性模型，为量子计算机的发展奠定了理论基础；1995年，他又提出了分布式量子计算模型，这一模型后来成为分布式量子算法和量子通信协议安全性的基础。

段路明教授现任密歇根大学教授、清华大学姚期智讲座教授，是组建量子信息物理实现团队的主要负责人之一。段教授是该领域的青年领军人物，他在量子网络、量子计算机、远距离量子通信及量子模拟等方面的物理实现研究已对量子信息领域产生了深远而广泛的影响。

量子信息中心借鉴国际一流高校和科研机构的管理机制，目前的研究方向包括全量子网络、量子计算、量子模拟、量子算法与复杂性理论、以及量子操作等。随着中心的进一步发展，其研究与合作也将拓展至更多与量子技术及信息安全相关的领域。

This webpage is the official introduction page for the **Center for Quantum Information (CQI)** at Tsinghua University's Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences (IIIS), also known as the "Quantum Center."

**About the Center:**
- Established on **January 6, 2011**, with an inauguration ceremony on **January 15, 2011**, at the FIT Building.
- Led by **Professor Andrew Chi-Chih Yao** (姚期智), a 2000 A.M. Turing Award winner and the first Asian scholar to receive the award. Yao pioneered quantum communication complexity theory (1993) and distributed quantum computing models (1995).
- **Professor Luming Duan** (段路明), a University of Michigan professor and Tsinghua Chair Professor, helps lead the physical implementation team, focusing on quantum networks, quantum computing, and long-distance quantum communication.
- Research directions include: **full quantum networks, quantum computing, quantum simulation, quantum algorithms & complexity theory, and quantum operations.**

**Faculty (selected):**
- Yao Qizhi (Andrew Yao) – Algorithms, cryptography, quantum computing, AI
- Duan Luming – Ion & superconducting quantum computing, quantum networks, quantum simulation, quantum AI
- Ma Xiongfeng – Quantum information science
- Sun Luyan – Superconducting quantum information processing
- Deng Dongling – Quantum AI, quantum information, topological phases
- Xu Yong – Quantum physics, nonlinear physics, quantum many-body physics
- Hou Panyu – Ion quantum computing, diamond color center applications
- Pu Yunfei – Ion trap quantum networks, neutral atom array quantum computing
- Wu Yukai – Physical implementation of quantum computing

**Notable Research Updates (2025–2026):**
- 05-28-2026: First observation of many-body dynamical freezing
- 01-28-2026: First experimental realization of high-encoding-rate quantum error correction codes
- 10-02-2025: Prof. Duan Luming received the 6th Beijing Overseas Chinese "Jinghua Award"
- 08-28-2025: *Nature* publication on novel quantum states on a 100-qubit quantum chip
- 01-24-2025: First high-fidelity quantum entanglement gate between dual-encoded qubits (Duan group)

**Notable Alumni:**
- Ma Yuwei (2022 PhD, advised by Sun Luyan) – Postdoc at Shanghai Branch of USTC; thesis awarded "Tsinghua Excellent Doctoral Dissertation."
- Tang Wenbin (2010 graduate, advised by Yao Qizhi) – Co-founder of Megvii (旷视科技).

姚班培养

清华学堂计算机科学实验班（简称“姚班”）由世界著名计算机科学家、2000年图灵奖得主姚期智院士于2005年创办，致力于培养国际顶尖计算机科学及交叉创新人才。二十年来姚班“最优秀的本科生和最优秀的本科教育”已经誉满全球。

姚班拥有一流教师团队，精心设计培育方案，提供丰富国际科研合作机会，着力打造世界顶尖人才培养平台。面向科技发展前沿和国家重大需求，提出最先进培养方案，设立计算机科学、人工智能和量子信息三大专业方向，供学生自由选择。姚期智院士精心设置覆盖计算机科学、人工智能、量子信息前沿领域的专业课程并亲自参与授课。

姚班的办学理念和办学成果得到了教育部的充分肯定与大力支持，为国内拔尖创新人才培养树立了突出典范。如今毕业生活跃于全球信息领域包括学术界及高新企业，正引领全球信息革命的创新浪潮。

姚班的信念是：由最优秀的老师，设计最先进的课程，教育出最出色的学生！我们热烈欢迎新同学加入姚班！

args.summary:
This is the homepage of the Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences (IIIS) at Tsinghua University, also known as the "Yao Class" (姚班) and the Quantum Information Center (CQI). The institute was founded by Turing Award winner Andrew Chi-Chih Yao (姚期智) in 2005 and is dedicated to cultivating top interdisciplinary talent in computer science, artificial intelligence, and quantum information science.

Key highlights from the page include:

**Recent News (as of mid-2026):**
- Professor Gao Yang was selected for MIT Technology Review's "35 Innovators Under 35" China list (July 2026).
- Professor Sun Luyan's research group, with collaborators, achieved a new framework for Fock space optical control (July 2026).
- IIIS held its 2026 graduation ceremony (June 2026).
- Andrew Yao, Yoshua Bengio, Zhang Yaqin, and Stuart Russell jointly signed the "IDAIS London Declaration" (June 2026).
- IIIS research team observed many-body dynamical freezing for the first time (May 2026).

**Yao Class (姚班):**
The Tsinghua Computer Science Experimental Class (姚班), founded in 2005 by Andrew Yao, is renowned for producing top undergraduate talent. It offers three major tracks: Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Quantum Information. The program has graduated 660+ undergraduates and 360+ graduate students cumulatively.

**Quantum Information Center (CQI):**
Led by Andrew Yao (academic leader) and Academician Duan Luming (executive director), the center focuses on quantum networks, quantum computing, quantum simulation, quantum algorithms, and related fields. It has published dozens of papers in top journals like Nature and Science.

**Key Statistics:**
- 5 alumni have won Sloan Research Fellowships
- 11 times students have won international top conference awards
- 4 graduate and 8 undergraduate Tsinghua Special Prize winners
- 32 high-level overseas talents recruited
- 610+ full-time students currently enrolled
- 360+ graduate students and 660+ undergraduate graduates cultivated

The institute's research areas span computer architecture, algorithms, cryptography, game theory; embodied AI, HCI, reinforcement learning, computer graphics/vision, multi-agent systems, AI safety; and quantum computing (ion trap, superconducting, neutral atom, diamond quantum networks, etc.).

Contact: FIT Building, Room 1-208, Tsinghua University, Haidian District, Beijing 100084 | Tel: 010-62781693 | Email: iiis@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn

**Scott Joel Aaronson** (born May 21, 1981) is an American [theoretical computer scientist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_computer_science "Theoretical computer science") and Schlumberger Centennial Chair of Computer Science at the [University of Texas at Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_at_Austin "University of Texas at Austin"). His primary areas of research are [computational complexity theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_complexity_theory "Computational complexity theory") and [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing "Quantum computing").

## Early life and education

[[edit source](/w/index.php?title=Scott_Aaronson&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section's source code: Early life and education")]

Aaronson grew up in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), though he spent a year in [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") when his father was posted to [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong").[[3]](#cite_note-MIT_bio-3) He enrolled in a school there that permitted him to skip ahead several years in math, but upon returning to the US, he had difficulties in school, getting bad grades and having run-ins with teachers. He enrolled in The Clarkson School, a [gifted education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gifted_education "Gifted education") program run by [Clarkson University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarkson_University "Clarkson University"), which enabled Aaronson to apply for colleges while only in his freshman year of high school.[[3]](#cite_note-MIT_bio-3) He was accepted into [Cornell University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University "Cornell University"), where he obtained his BSc in [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science") in 2000,[[4]](#cite_note-vita-4) and where he resided at the [Telluride House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telluride_House "Telluride House").[[5]](#cite_note-Aaronson-Quickies-5) He then attended the [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley"), for his PhD, which he got in 2004 under the supervision of [Umesh Vazirani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Vazirani "Umesh Vazirani").[[6]](#cite_note-6)

As a child, Aaronson was particularly interested in mathematics. In part due to this, he felt drawn to theoretical computing, particularly [computational complexity theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_complexity_theory "Computational complexity theory"). At Cornell, he became interested in quantum computing and devoted himself to computational complexity and quantum computing.[[3]](#cite_note-MIT_bio-3)

## Career

[[edit source](/w/index.php?title=Scott_Aaronson&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section's source code: Career")]

After [postdoctorates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postdoctorate "Postdoctorate") at the [Institute for Advanced Study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Advanced_Study "Institute for Advanced Study") and the [University of Waterloo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Waterloo "University of Waterloo"), he took a faculty position at MIT in 2007.[[4]](#cite_note-vita-4) His primary area of research is quantum computing and computational complexity theory more generally.

In the summer of 2016 he moved from MIT to the [University of Texas at Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_at_Austin "University of Texas at Austin") as David J. Bruton Jr. Centennial Professor of Computer Sciences #2 and as the founding director of UT Austin's new Quantum Information Center.[[7]](#cite_note-fromboston-7) In summer 2022 he announced he would be working for a year at [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI") on theoretical foundations of [AI safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_safety "AI safety").[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) He worked at the company for two years.[[10]](#cite_note-goldman2025a-10)

## Popular work

[[edit source](/w/index.php?title=Scott_Aaronson&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section's source code: Popular work")]

He is a founder of the *Complexity Zoo* [wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiki "Wiki"), which catalogs all classes of [computational complexity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_complexity_theory "Computational complexity theory").[[11]](#cite_note-11)[[12]](#cite_note-12) He is the author of the blog "Shtetl-Optimized".[[13]](#cite_note-scottaaronson-13)

In a *[Scientific American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_American "Scientific American")* interview he answers why his blog is called *shtetl-optimized*, and explains his preoccupation with the past:

> [Shtetls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shtetl "Shtetl") were Jewish villages in pre-[Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust "Holocaust") Eastern Europe. They're where all my ancestors came from—some actually from the same place ([Vitebsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitebsk "Vitebsk")) as [Marc Chagall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Chagall "Marc Chagall"), who painted the [fiddler on the roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddler_on_the_roof "Fiddler on the roof"). I watched Fiddler many times as a kid, both the movie and the play. And every time, there was a jolt of recognition, like: "So that's the world I was designed to inhabit. All the aspects of my personality that mark me out as weird today, the obsessive reading and the literal-mindedness and even the rocking back and forth—I probably have them because back then they would've made me a better [Talmud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talmud "Talmud") scholar, or something."

— Scott Aaronson[[14]](#cite_note-14)

He also wrote the essay "Who Can Name The Bigger Number?".[[15]](#cite_note-15) The latter work, widely distributed in academic [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science"), uses the concept of [Busy Beaver Numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busy_Beaver_Number "Busy Beaver Number") as described by [Tibor Radó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibor_Radó "Tibor Radó") to illustrate the limits of [computability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computability "Computability") in a pedagogic environment.

He has also taught a graduate-level survey course, "Quantum Computing Since Democritus",[[16]](#cite_note-scottaaronson2-16) for which notes are available online, and have been published as a book by [Cambridge University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_University_Press "Cambridge University Press").[[17]](#cite_note-cambridge-17) It weaves together disparate topics into a cohesive whole, including [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics "Quantum mechanics"), complexity, free will, [time travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel "Time travel"), the [anthropic principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic_principle "Anthropic principle") and more. Many of these interdisciplinary applications of computational complexity were later fleshed out in his article, "Why Philosophers Should Care About Computational Complexity".[[18]](#cite_note-whycare-2011-18) Since then, Aaronson published a book entitled *[Quantum Computing Since Democritus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_Computing_Since_Democritus "Quantum Computing Since Democritus")* based on the course.

An article of Aaronson's, "The Limits of Quantum Computers", was published in *[Scientific American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_American "Scientific American")*,[[19]](#cite_note-sciam-2008-19) and he was a [guest speaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guest_speaker "Guest speaker") at the 2007 [Foundational Questions in Science Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundational_Questions_in_Science_Institute "Foundational Questions in Science Institute") conference.[[20]](#cite_note-20) Aaronson is frequently cited in the non-academic press, such as *[Science News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_News "Science News"),*[[21]](#cite_note-21) *[The Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Age "The Age"),*[[22]](#cite_note-22) [ZDNet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZDNet "ZDNet"),[[23]](#cite_note-23) *[Slashdot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slashdot "Slashdot"),*[[24]](#cite_note-24) *[New Scientist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Scientist "New Scientist"),*[[25]](#cite_note-25) *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times"),*[[26]](#cite_note-nyt-26) and *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* magazine.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

## Awards

[[edit source](/w/index.php?title=Scott_Aaronson&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section's source code: Awards")]

* Aaronson is one of two winners of the 2012 [Alan T. Waterman Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_T._Waterman_Award "Alan T. Waterman Award").[[28]](#cite_note-28)
* Best Student Paper Awards at the [Computational Complexity Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_Complexity_Conference "Computational Complexity Conference") for the papers "Limitations of Quantum Advice and One-Way Communication" (2004) [[29]](#cite_note-29) and "Quantum Certificate Complexity" (2003).[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31)
* Danny Lewin Best Student Paper Award at the [Symposium on Theory of Computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symposium_on_Theory_of_Computing "Symposium on Theory of Computing") for the paper "Lower Bounds for Local Search by Quantum Arguments" (2004).[[32]](#cite_note-32)
* 2009 [Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Early_Career_Award_for_Scientists_and_Engineers "Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers")[[33]](#cite_note-33)
* 2009 [Sloan Research Fellowship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloan_Research_Fellowship "Sloan Research Fellowship")[[34]](#cite_note-34)
* 2017 [Simons Investigator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simons_Investigator "Simons Investigator")[[35]](#cite_note-35)
* He was elected as an [ACM Fellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACM_Fellow "ACM Fellow") in 2019 "for contributions to quantum computing and computational complexity".[[36]](#cite_note-36)
* He was awarded the 2020 ACM Prize in Computing "for groundbreaking contributions to quantum computing".[[37]](#cite_note-37)
* He was elected to the [US National Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Sciences "National Academy of Sciences") in 2026.[[38]](#cite_note-c425-38)
* Inaugural 2026 Luca Trevisan Award for Expository Work from [ACM SIGACT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACM_SIGACT "ACM SIGACT")[[39]](#cite_note-39)

## Personal life

[[edit source](/w/index.php?title=Scott_Aaronson&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section's source code: Personal life")]

Aaronson is married to computer scientist [Dana Moshkovitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Moshkovitz "Dana Moshkovitz").[[7]](#cite_note-fromboston-7) Aaronson is [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews"),[[40]](#cite_note-40)[[41]](#cite_note-41)[[42]](#cite_note-42) and has described himself as "radicalized in my Jewish and Zionist identities".[[43]](#cite_note-43)

args.summary:
Scott Aaronson (born May 21, 1981) is an American theoretical computer scientist and Schlumberger Centennial Chair of Computer Science at the University of Texas at Austin, specializing in computational complexity theory and quantum computing. He earned his BSc from Cornell University (2000) and PhD from UC Berkeley (2004) under Umesh Vazirani. After postdoctorates at the Institute for Advanced Study and University of Waterloo, he joined MIT's faculty in 2007 before moving to UT Austin in 2016 as founding director of the Quantum Information Center. In 2022, he began working at OpenAI on AI safety, remaining there for two years.

Aaronson is known for his work on PostBQP (quantum Turing machine with postselection), algebrization, and boson sampling. He founded the Complexity Zoo wiki, writes the blog "Shtetl-Optimized," and authored the book "Quantum Computing Since Democritus." His notable awards include the Alan T. Waterman Award (2012), Presidential Early Career Award (2009), Sloan Research Fellowship (2009), Simons Investigator (2017), ACM Fellow (2019), ACM Prize in Computing (2020), and election to the US National Academy of Sciences (2026). He is married to computer scientist Dana Moshkovitz and is Jewish.

args.summary: Scott Aaronson is a Professor at UT Austin, previously teaching at MIT for nine years in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. His primary research area is theoretical computer science, focusing on the capabilities and limits of quantum computers and computational complexity theory. Key publications include "Quantum Computing Since Democritus" (2013, Cambridge University Press) and several papers on quantum query complexity, quantum lower bounds, and online learning of quantum states. He has received numerous awards: the ACM Prize in Computing (2021), Tomassoni-Chisesi Award (2018), Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship (2016), Alan T. Waterman Award (2012), US Presidential Early Career Award (2010), and a Sloan Research Fellowship (2009), among others. He holds the David Bruton, Jr. Centennial Professorship in Computer Sciences #2 at UT Austin. Related recent news includes his election to the National Academy of Sciences, election as AAAS Fellow, and a quantum breakthrough in certified randomness.

# UT Austin Computer Scientist Elected to National Academy of Sciences

April 29, 2026 • by Marc Airhart

Scott Aaronson, a renowned quantum computing expert, joins the country’s most prestigious scientific organization.

![Portrait of a scientist with glasses. In the background is a computer integrated circuit board.](/sites/default/files/uploads/images/default/scottaaronson-01.jpg)

---

Scott Aaronson, a professor of computer science at The University of Texas at Austin, was elected this week to the National Academy of Sciences. The academy is the country’s most prestigious scientific organization, and election to it is one of the highest honors for American researchers.

Aaronson, the Schlumberger Centennial Chair of Computer Science, is [one of 120 members and 25 international members inducted this year](https://www.nasonline.org/news/2026-nas-election/) at the 163rd Annual Meeting of the NAS in recognition of distinguished and continuing achievements in original scientific research.

“It's gratifying to receive an honor like this,” Aaronson said. “I especially feel grateful to all the colleagues, mentors, and students I've worked with over the years, who believed in me and helped me.”

A graduate of Cornell University, Aaronson earned a Ph.D. in computer science from the University of California, Berkeley. Following stints as a postdoctoral researcher at the Institute for Advanced Study and the University of Waterloo, and as a faculty member at the Massachusetts Institute for Technology, he joined the UT faculty in 2016.

His research interests center around the capabilities and limits of quantum computers and computational complexity theory more generally. Quantum computers use the principles of physics at the smallest scales to process information in fundamentally different ways than ordinary computers.

Aaronson helped develop the concept of quantum supremacy, the milestone at which a quantum device can solve a problem that no classical computer can solve in a reasonable amount of time. He established many of the theoretical foundations of quantum supremacy experiments. Such experiments allow scientists to give convincing evidence that quantum computers provide exponential speedups without having to first build a full fault-tolerant quantum computer.

Aaronson’s previous honors include the [ACM Prize in Computing](https://awards.acm.org/acm-prize) (2020), the [Tomassoni-Chisesi Prize in Physics](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/news/2018/scott-aaronson-awarded-tomassoni-chisesi-physics-prize-quantum-computing-research) (2018), a [Simons Investigator Award](https://cns.utexas.edu/news/quantum-computer-scientist-named-simons-foundation-investigator) (2017) and the [Alan T. Waterman Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_T._Waterman_Award) of the National Science Foundation (2012).

Beyond his technical contributions, Aaronson has become recognized as a leading spokesperson for the field. He maintains a popular blog, [Shtetl Optimized](https://www.scottaaronson.com/blog/), where he explains timely and exciting topics in computing. He also authored *Quantum Computing Since Democritus*, a highly respected book on quantum computing. And he has written several articles for popular science audiences and presented a TED Talk at TEDxDresden to dispel misconceptions and provide the public with a more accurate overview of the field.

The [National Academy of Sciences](http://www.nasonline.org/) is a private, nonprofit institution that was established under a congressional charter signed by President Abraham Lincoln in 1863. The academy recognizes achievement in science by election to membership, and—with the National Academy of Engineering and the National Academy of Medicine—provides science, engineering and health policy advice to the federal government and other organizations. Aaronson is one of [25 faculty members](https://cns.utexas.edu/about-the-college/facts-and-rankings/faculty-research-awards) in the College of Natural Sciences across the National Academies.

He is one of 120 members and 25 international members inducted this year at the NAS's 163rd Annual Meeting. Aaronson holds the Schlumberger Centennial Chair of Computer Science and joined UT Austin in 2016 after previous roles at MIT, the University of Waterloo, the Institute for Advanced Study, and UC Berkeley. His research focuses on quantum computing and computational complexity theory. He helped develop the concept of quantum supremacy and established many of its theoretical foundations. His previous honors include the ACM Prize in Computing (2020), Tomassoni-Chisesi Prize in Physics (2018), Simons Investigator Award (2017), and the Alan T. Waterman Award (2012). args.summary:
The Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics (MPQ), founded in 1981 and located in Garching bei München, Germany, is a leading research organization focused on quantum science, photonics, laser physics, and precision experiments centered on light-matter interaction. It employs 201-500 people with 250 associated LinkedIn members. The institute conducts research across five lines of inquiry, supported by world-class infrastructure and laboratories. Key specialties include Quantum Optics, Laserspectroscopy, Quantum Many Body Systems, Quantum Information, Attosecond Physics, Photonics, and Quantum Entanglement.

Recent notable developments include:
- Director Ignacio Cirac received his 10th honorary doctorate from Universidad Carlos III de Madrid for pioneering contributions to quantum information theory.
- Alumna Amelie Heinzerling received the Otto Hahn Medal from the Max Planck Society for her thesis on field-resolved single-cycle deep-UV pulses via attosecond solitons, published in Nature Photonics.
- A public lecture (July 2026) by Moritz Dorband on "The Search for the One Theory" exploring why gravity doesn't fit the Standard Model.
- The Atomic Quantum Matter Conference (September 7-11, 2026, at ISTA Austria) is accepting poster abstracts until June 15.
- Upcoming events: Girls for Science (July 24, 2026) at MPQ, and a public talk on quantum computing by Prof. Christopher Monroe (June 17, 2026, at Deutsches Museum).
- Research by Jad C. Halimee published in Science Magazine on observing disorder-free localization using a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on Google's quantum processor.
- Ferenc Krausz is working on applying attosecond laser techniques to medical applications for early disease detection (cancer, diabetes) via molecular fingerprinting in blood samples.

Similar organizations include Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, Munich Center for Quantum Science and Technology (MCQST), Niels Bohr Institute, and Munich Quantum Valley.

The **Max-Planck-Institute of Quantum Optics** (abbreviation: **MPQ**; [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): ***Max-Planck-Institut für Quantenoptik***) is a part of the [Max Planck Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Planck_Society "Max Planck Society") which operates 87 research facilities in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany").

The institute is located in [Garching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garching "Garching"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), which in turn is located 10 km north-east of [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"). Five research groups work in the fields of [attosecond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attosecond "Attosecond") physics, [laser physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_physics "Laser physics"), [quantum information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information "Quantum information") theory, [laser spectroscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_spectroscopy "Laser spectroscopy"), quantum dynamics and quantum many body systems.

## Research

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Planck_Institute_of_Quantum_Optics&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Research")]

The institute investigates the interaction of light and matter. Its faculty members conduct research in topics such as theoretical quantum optics, [quantum information theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information_theory "Quantum information theory"), ultra-high-resolution laser spectroscopy, quantum physics of ultra-cold atoms, development of components for [quantum computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer "Quantum computer") and quantum networks, [Bose Einstein condensation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bose_Einstein_condensation?action=edit&redlink=1 "Bose Einstein condensation (page does not exist)") of degenerate quantum gases, attosecond physics, development of new radiation and particle sources for fundamental and medical applications, etc. There used to be a group at MPQ that conducted experiments on [gravitational waves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravitational_wave "Gravitational wave").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Planck_Institute_of_Quantum_Optics&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: History")]

The Max-Planck-Institute for Quantum Optics was founded on January 1, 1981. It was a successor of a project group for laser research of the [Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Planck_Institute_for_Plasma_Physics "Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics"). The use of lasers for [fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fusion_power "Fusion power") research, quantum optics and spectroscopy were the goals of the project group, which was established in 1976 and consisted of 46 members. In 1981 the staff numbers had risen to 82 and the institute was comprising the divisions of Laser Physics (Prof. [Herbert Walther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Walther "Herbert Walther")), Laser Chemistry (Prof. Karl-Ludwig Kompa) and Laser Plasma (Dr. Siegbert Witkowski).

The institute was initially accommodated on the premises of the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, but eventually moved to its new building in July 1986, officially separating from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics. With the appointment of [Theodor Hänsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Hänsch "Theodor Hänsch") (then at [Stanford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University "Stanford University")) as new director, the institute grew significantly. Hänsch established the Laser Spectroscopy Division and was also given a chair at [LMU Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMU_Munich "LMU Munich"), which ensured close links between MPQ and the university complex in Munich. After the retirement of Siegbert Witkowski in 1993, the research on the high energy laser was stopped and other research areas were started.

In 1999 Professor [Gerhard Rempe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Rempe "Gerhard Rempe") (then [University of Constance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Constance "University of Constance")) was appointed as director at the MPQ, and the Quantum Dynamics Division was set up.

In 2001 the Research Group on [Gravitational Waves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravitational_Waves "Gravitational Waves"), led by Dr. Karsten Danzmann, moved to Hanover where the first test measurements were carried out in the experiment. Since then that group has been a part of the [MPI for Gravitational Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPI_for_Gravitational_Physics "MPI for Gravitational Physics") (Potsdam) that was founded in 1995.[[2]](#cite_note-2) In the same year (2001) Professor Ignacio Cirac (then [University of Innsbruck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Innsbruck "University of Innsbruck")) accepted a call as director at the MPQ and set up the first Theory Division at the institute.

At the beginning of 2003 Professor Herbert Walther acquired emeritus status, but continued his research work as head of the Laser Physics Emeritus Group until his death in July 2006. His successor as director at the MPQ and professor at the LMU is Professor Ferenc Krausz (previously [Technical University of Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_University_of_Vienna "Technical University of Vienna")). Professor Krausz has led the Attosecond Physics Division since 2003.

Professor Karl-Ludwig Kompa was the last founding father of the institute to retire in 2006. In parallel with these retirements three new research divisions and several independent research groups were established: In 2004 the Attosecond Driver Laser Group was formed, whose leader Dr. Andrius Baltuska took up a professorship at the Technical University of Vienna in 2006. The same year also the Quantum Simulations with Trapped Ions Group was founded, led by Dr. Tobias Schätz (now at the [University of Freiburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Freiburg "University of Freiburg")). In 2005 Dr. Tobias Kippenberg (now at the [Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecole_Polytechnique_Fédérale_de_Lausanne "Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne")) set up his Laboratory of Photonics at the MPQ. In 2006 Dr. Reinhard Kienberger (now at the [Technical University of Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_University_of_Munich "Technical University of Munich")) received funding to set up the research group Attosecond Dynamics. In 2007 a further research group was founded, on Attosecond Imaging, led by Dr. Matthias Kling. In January 2008 Dr. Masaki Hori established his group on Antimatter Spectroscopy, followed by the Ultrafast Quantum Optics group of Dr. Peter Hommelhoff (now at the [University of Erlangen-Nuremberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Erlangen-Nuremberg "University of Erlangen-Nuremberg")) in April 2008. In December 2010 Dr. [Elefterios Goulielmakis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleftherios_Goulielmakis "Eleftherios Goulielmakis") (now at the [University of Rostock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Rostock "University of Rostock")) started his research group on Attoelectronics. Dr. Randolf Pohl (now at the [University of Mainz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Mainz "University of Mainz")) started to establish his research group "[Muonic Atoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muonic_Atoms "Muonic Atoms")" at the end of 2011. Currently (in February 2020), there exist five independent research groups at MPQ. In addition to Masaki Hori's antimatter spectroscopy group, there is the Rydberg Dressed Quantum Many-Body Systems Group (Dr. Christian Groß), the Otto Hahn Group on Quantum Networks (Dr. Andreas Reiserer), the Theory of Quantum Matter Group (Dr. Richard Schmidt), and the Entanglement of Complex Quantum Systems Group (Prof. Dr. Norbert Schuch).[[3]](#cite_note-3)

In 2005, [Theodor W. Hänsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_W._Hänsch "Theodor W. Hänsch") was awarded the [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"), together with [John L. Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_L._Hall "John L. Hall"), *"for their contributions to the development of laser-based precision spectroscopy, including the optical frequency comb technique"*. The [frequency comb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency_comb "Frequency comb") the Nobel Prize is referring to has been developed in his Laser Spectroscopy Division in the late 1990s.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

On 1 August 2008 a fifth division Quantum Many Body Systems was established by Prof. [Immanuel Bloch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immanuel_Bloch "Immanuel Bloch"). Prof. Bloch is successor of Prof. Theodor W. Hänsch, who normally would have retired as director at MPQ in 2009. Due to special agreements Prof. Hänsch will remain professor at the LMU and director at the MPQ at least until 2016. One research focus of Prof. Bloch is the investigation of ultracold quantum gases in [optical lattices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_lattice "Optical lattice"). These systems may help to model solid states and to get a better understanding of special properties such as e.g. [high temperature superconductivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_temperature_superconductivity "High temperature superconductivity").[[5]](#cite_note-5)

In 2023, Ferenc Krausz, Director at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Professor at LMU Munich, together with Pierre Agostini and Anne L'Huillier were honoured with the Nobel Prize in Physics. The Nobel Committee is honouring the three researchers for the foundation of attosecond physics.

args.summary:
The Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics (MPQ) is a research institute located in Garching near Munich, Germany, and is part of the Max Planck Society. Founded on January 1, 1981, it originated from a laser research project group at the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics. The institute employs approximately 400 staff members and its current managing director is Ferenc Krausz.

**Structure & Divisions:** The institute has five main research divisions: Attosecond physics (led by Ferenc Krausz), Laser spectroscopy (Theodor W. Hänsch), Quantum dynamics (Gerhard Rempe), Quantum many body systems (Immanuel Bloch), and Theory (Juan Ignacio Cirac Sasturain). Additionally, there are five independent research groups focusing on areas such as Rydberg Dressed Quantum Many-Body Systems, Antimatter spectroscopy, Quantum Networks, Theory of Quantum Matter, and Entanglement of Complex Quantum Systems.

**Research Focus:** MPQ investigates the interaction of light and matter, covering topics including theoretical quantum optics, quantum information theory, ultra-high-resolution laser spectroscopy, quantum physics of ultra-cold atoms, quantum computer components, Bose-Einstein condensation, attosecond physics, and development of new radiation/particle sources for fundamental and medical applications.

**Notable Achievements:** Two Nobel Prizes are associated with the institute: Theodor W. Hänsch received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2005 for contributions to laser-based precision spectroscopy (including the optical frequency comb technique), and Ferenc Krausz was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2023 (along with Pierre Agostini and Anne L'Huillier) for founding attosecond physics.

**History:** The institute grew from 46 members in 1976 to 82 in 1981, and moved to its own building in July 1986. Key appointments include Herbert Walther (Laser Physics), Karl-Ludwig Kompa (Laser Chemistry), and Theodor Hänsch (Laser Spectroscopy). The institute has strong affiliations with LMU Munich and the Technical University of Munich.

**Degree Programmes:** MPQ offers two PhD programmes: the International Max-Planck Research School (IMPRS) on Advanced Photon Science, and the International PhD Programme of Excellence on Quantum Computing, Control and Communication.

Named after Max Planck, who introduced the revolutionary quantum hypothesis in 1900, the Max Planck Society is Germany’s premier organisation for basic research. args.summary:
The Max Planck Quantum Alliance website serves as a central resource for exploring quantum science and technology research groups within the Max Planck Society, Germany's premier basic research organization named after Max Planck (who introduced the quantum hypothesis in 1900). The site covers seven key research areas: Quantum Communication, Quantum Computation, Quantum Simulation, Quantum Information Theory, Quantum Materials, Quantum Devices, and Quantum Sensing.

The page provides a comprehensive list of additional resources, including:
- Max Planck Distinguished Speaker Series on Quantum Computing and Quantum Information
- Max Planck Graduate Center for Quantum Materials
- Max Planck School of Photonics (covering quantum optics)
- Munich Quantum Valley (Bavarian quantum computing initiative involving two Max Planck Institutes)
- Multiple International Max Planck Research Schools (IMPRS) in related fields across Munich, Erlangen, Hamburg, Tübingen/Stuttgart, Stuttgart, Dresden, Halle, and Leipzig

The site also lists Max Planck Institutes with research groups working on quantum science and technology, spanning locations in Stuttgart, Garching, Erlangen, Dresden, Halle, Bochum, Tübingen/Stuttgart, Saarbrücken, Hamburg, and Leipzig.

Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics

## Pioneering in Quantum Optics

The MPQ is one of the world’s leading institutes in quantum optics. As part of the Max Planck Society, we provide our researchers with a unique infrastructure: state-of-the-art laboratories with first-class equipment, custom-made products from our in-house precision mechanical workshop, and an outstanding technical and administrative support.Excellent support that pays off - MPQ scientists publish around 200 papers a year, many of them in top-tier journals such as Nature and Science.

## Our task to train and teach

We are committed to training the next generation of scientists. We give our PhD students and postdocs the best possible support, so that many doors are open to them in academia and industry after their time at the MPQ. We also strive to inspire and engage the general public in quantum optics, starting with the very young, who can conduct quantum physics experiments in the PhotonLab, our student laboratory at MPQ. For everyone else, we regularly organise public events with popular science talks and laboratory tours.

## smart, diverse and likeable

The MPQ owes its leading position to its staff. We are fortunate to be able to attract the best researchers from around the world. More than 40 nations are currently represented at the MPQ. But it is not just skills that count for us, it is also character. Treating each other with respect is just as important to us as making sure the people who work here feel comfortable. That is why we are creating more and more opportunities to get to know people outside the lab and the workplace.

## Gates to uncharted territory

Quantum physics is the great scientific revelation of the 20th century. Through it, we observe phenomena that often defy our intuition and completely turn our understanding of nature upside down. In short, phenomena that push us to the limits of our knowledge. With our fundamental research at the MPQ, we are gradually opening the gates to a new physics that has the potential to change our world, our knowledge and our technologies forever. Five research areas are currently established at the MPQ.

## An excellent environment

The MPQ is part of the Garching research campus, one of the strongest scientific regions in Germany. Garching is located in close proximity to the cultural city of Munich, the Bavarian countryside and the Alps. Our environment is also scientifically excellent: we maintain close links with the elite universities located here, LMU and TU Munich, and internationally with top institutions such as Harvard, MIT and Stanford. We are also host to leading scientists from all over the world, who visit us as guests and speakers on a daily basis.

## The Nobel Prize Award Ceremony 2023 in Stockholm

What a special moment for our dear Ferenc Krausz! On Sunday 10 December, he, Anne L'Huillier (Lund University) and Pierre Agostini (Ohio State University) were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for the foundation of attosecond physics. Here, the King of Sweden, Carl XVI Gustav, presents the Nobel Medal to Ferenc Krausz in Stockholm.

[## A Nobel Prize for the Attosecond!

A billionth of a billionth of a second - ultrafast light pulses make it possible to study in real time some of the fastest processes in nature - the movement of electrons in atoms and molecules. Ferenc Krausz is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for this masterstroke. Our dearest congratulations! She was recognized for her pioneering contributions to ultrafast optics and attosecond science. The award ceremony took place during the Max Planck Society's Annual Meeting in Frankfurt am Main.

# Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics (MPQ) - Summary

The Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics (MPQ) in Garching, Germany (near Munich), is one of the world's leading institutes in quantum optics, part of the Max Planck Society. It provides state-of-the-art laboratories, in-house precision mechanical workshops, and strong administrative support. MPQ scientists publish around 200 papers annually, many in top-tier journals.

## Key Achievements
- **Ferenc Krausz**, MPQ Director, was awarded the **2023 Nobel Prize in Physics** (with Anne L'Huillier and Pierre Agostini) for founding attosecond physics—using ultrafast light pulses to study electron movement in atoms and molecules.
- **Ignacio Cirac**, Director of the Theory Division, received an honorary doctorate from Universidad Carlos III de Madrid for pioneering contributions to quantum information theory.
- Krausz was elected as an international member of the American National Academy of Sciences (NAS) in April 2026.

## Recent News (2026)
- **Otto Hahn Medal (June 23, 2026)**: Awarded to Amelie Heinzerling for ultrafast optics and attosecond science research.
- **European Quantum Academy (June 16, 2026)**: MPQ PhotonLab became a partner in the EU Quantum Flagship project to coordinate quantum education across Europe.
- **The Attochamber (June 2, 2026)**: Film and photo materials produced at the Nobel Prize Museum featuring the historic experimental setup used to generate the first attosecond light pulses in 2001.
- **Girls' Day 2026 (April 24, 2026)**: 16 female students participated in hands-on quantum optics research activities.

## Research & Education
- Five established research areas in fundamental quantum physics.
- **PhotonLab**: Student laboratory for conducting quantum physics experiments, open to the public.
- Diverse workforce with over 40 nations represented.
- Strong collaborations with LMU Munich, TU Munich, Harvard, MIT, and Stanford.
- Upcoming events include "Atomic Quantum Matter" conference (Sept 7-11, 2026), Quantum Tuesdays at Deutsches Museum, and Quantum Fridays at PhotonLab.

## Latest Publications (2026)
- Phase-Sensitive Measurements on a Fermi–Hubbard Quantum Processor (May 12)
- Disorder-Free Localization and Fragmentation in a Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory (April 30)
- State preparation with parallel-sequential circuits (April 21)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

French institute for mathematics and theoretical physics

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/IHES_main_building.jpg/250px-IHES_main_building.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:IHES_main_building.jpg)

IHÉS main building

The **Institut des hautes études scientifiques** (**IHÉS**; English: Institute of Advanced Scientific Studies) is a French [research institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_institute "Research institute") supporting advanced research in mathematics and [theoretical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physics "Theoretical physics") (also with a small theoretical biology group). It is located in [Bures-sur-Yvette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bures-sur-Yvette "Bures-sur-Yvette"), just south of [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"). It is an independently governed research institute and a founding member of the [University of Paris-Saclay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris-Saclay "University of Paris-Saclay").

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Institut_des_hautes_%C3%A9tudes_scientifiques&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The IHÉS was founded in 1958 by businessman and mathematical physicist [Léon Motchane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Léon_Motchane "Léon Motchane") with the help of [Robert Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Oppenheimer "Robert Oppenheimer") and [Jean Dieudonné](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Dieudonné "Jean Dieudonné") as a research centre in France, modeled on the renowned [Institute for Advanced Study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Advanced_Study "Institute for Advanced Study") in Princeton, United States.[[1]](#cite_note-50th_anniversary-1)

> IHÉS deeply draws inspiration from the model of the esteemed Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton (IAS). ... IHÉS adopted its basic characteristics – the intellectual ones – as a high level institute dedicated to basic research – and certain practical ones – such as the tradition of tea being served daily, conducive to exchanges of views. Of equal importance was the relationship between Oppenheimer and Léon Motchane (1900–1990), the founder and first director of IHÉS. As life member of the scientific committee, advisor to the director, frequent visitor and regular correspondent, Oppenheimer played a major role in the crucial early years at IHÉS. ... Oppenheimer and Motchane ... exchanged long letters and short telegrams on all aspects of life at IHÉS. ... Visits by Oppenheimer were cleverly orchestrated by Léon Motchane and reported in the press. Oppenheimer's presence was an event in itself and his coming to lHÉS gave the Institute important official recognition. Oppenheimer was to come to IHÉS three times: from 16 to 19 September 1959, on 17 and 18 October 1961 (in Bures, although the Institute had not moved there yet), and from 14 to 17 May 1963. His last visit, planned for 1965, was cancelled for health reasons.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

The strong personality of [Alexander Grothendieck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Grothendieck "Alexander Grothendieck") and the broad sweep of his revolutionizing theories were a dominating feature of the first ten years at the IHÉS.[[3]](#cite_note-3) [René Thom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/René_Thom "René Thom") received an invitation from IHÉS in 1963 and, after his appointment, remained there until his death in 2002.[[4]](#cite_note-4) [Dennis Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Sullivan "Dennis Sullivan") is remembered as one who had a special talent for encouraging exchanges among visitors and provoking new and deeper insights into their ideas.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

The IHÉS runs a highly regarded mathematical journal, *[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publications_Mathématiques_de_l'IHÉS "Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS")*.

IHÉS celebrated its 40th anniversary in 1998[[5]](#cite_note-5) and its 50th in 2008.[[1]](#cite_note-50th_anniversary-1)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

## Scientists associated with the IHES

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Institut_des_hautes_%C3%A9tudes_scientifiques&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Scientists associated with the IHES")]

[Alain Connes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Connes "Alain Connes") (Fields Medal 1982) has held the Léon Motchane Chair since 1979. Several [CNRS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_national_de_la_recherche_scientifique "Centre national de la recherche scientifique") researchers are also based at the IHES: [Ahmed Abbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Abbes "Ahmed Abbes"), [Thierry Baudineau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Baudineau?action=edit&redlink=1 "Thierry Baudineau (page does not exist)"), [Ofer Gabber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ofer_Gabber "Ofer Gabber"), [Fanny Kassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Kassel "Fanny Kassel") and [Christophe Soulé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christophe_Soulé "Christophe Soulé") in mathematics and [Clément Delcamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Delcamp?action=edit&redlink=1 "Clément Delcamp (page does not exist)") in physics. [Yilin Wang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yilin_Wang "Yilin Wang") is a junior professor.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

args.summary:
The Institut des hautes études scientifiques (IHÉS; Institute of Advanced Scientific Studies) is a French research institute located in Bures-sur-Yvette, just south of Paris, focused on advanced research in mathematics and theoretical physics (with a small theoretical biology group). It is a founding member of the University of Paris-Saclay and an independently governed research institute.

**History:** Founded in 1958 by businessman Léon Motchane with help from Robert Oppenheimer and Jean Dieudonné, modeled after the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. Alexander Grothendieck's revolutionary theories dominated the first ten years. René Thom joined in 1963 and remained until his death in 2002. The institute publishes the highly regarded journal *Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS*.

**Directors:**
- Léon Motchane (1958–1971)
- Nicolaas Kuiper (1971–1985)
- Marcel Berger (1985–1994)
- Jean-Pierre Bourguignon (1994–2013)
- Emmanuel Ullmo (2013–present)

**Notable Permanent Professors (past and present):** Alexander Grothendieck (Fields Medal 1966), René Thom (Fields Medal 1958), Pierre Deligne (Fields Medal 1978, Abel Prize 2013), Dennis Sullivan (Wolf Prize 2010, Abel Prize 2022), Mikhail Gromov (Wolf Prize 1993, Abel Prize 2009), Jean Bourgain (Fields Medal 1994), Maxim Kontsevich (Fields Medal 1998), Laurent Lafforgue (Fields Medal 2002), Hugo Duminil-Copin (Fields Medal 2022), and others. Current permanent professors include Maxim Kontsevich, Hugo Duminil-Copin, Slava Rychkov, Laure Saint-Raymond, Dustin Clausen, Julio Parra-Martinez, and Hong Wang (joining 2025).

# Invited researchers

The visitor programme represents the institute’s most important scientific activity. Each year, around 200 researchers are selected by the Scientific Council, after an application procedure. Drawn by the spontaneous and sometimes unexpected interactions that the Institute makes possible and encourages, visitors stay on average for 2.5 months.  
 Triennial chairs provide considerable flexibility for organising scientific activities, with the possibility of inviting collaborators and organising events, and chair holders can stay for longer periods at the Institute.  
  
 [Apply](/applications/)

## The Schlumberger Chair for Mathematical Sciences

This chair was created in 2006 thanks to the trust and support of Schlumberger and is dedicated to topics at the interface with high technology. [More information](https://www.ihes.fr/en/scholars/invited-researchers/associated-professorships/schlumberger-chair-former-holders/).

* ### [Carlos Kenig, Mathematics](https://www.ihes.fr/en/professeur/carlos-kenig-2/)

  **Schlumberger Chair for Mathematical Sciences**

  Carlos E. Kenig, an internationally renowned mathematician, is recognized for his pioneering contributions to harmonic analysis and partial differential equations, particularly in the study of nonlinear dispersive equations.

  * ### [Jesse Thaler, Mathematics](https://www.ihes.fr/en/professeur/jesse-thaler/)

    **Schlumberger Chair for Mathematical Sciences**

    Jesse Thaler, a theoretical physicist at MIT and holder of the Schlumberger Chair at IHES, works at the intersection of quantum field theory and artificial intelligence, developing new approaches to uncover the mysteries of fundamental physics.

    * ### [Yves Barral, Theoretical Biology](https://www.ihes.fr/en/professeur/yves-barral/)

      **Schlumberger Chair for Mathematical Sciences**

      Yves Barral works in biology, guided by the question of the links between mathematics and biology, and why these links remain confused and little explored.

      * ### [Clément Mouhot, mathematician](https://www.ihes.fr/en/professeur/mouhot-clement/)

        **Schlumberger Chair for Mathematical Sciences**

        Clément Mouhot is a professor of mathematics at the University of Cambridge. He is interested in the mathematical analysis of the foundations of statistical mechanics, at the interface of partial differential equations, probabilities, and functional inequalities.

        * ### [Pierre Raphael, mathematician](https://www.ihes.fr/en/professeur/pierre-raphael/)

          **The Schlumberger Chair for Mathematical Sciences**

          Pierre Raphael is the Herchel Smith Professor of Pure Mathematics at the Faculty of Mathematics of Cambridge.  
             
           His research on non-linear partial differential equations aims at the description of energy concentration mechanisms and singularity formation during the propagation of non-linear waves

            **The Schlumberger Chair for Mathematical Sciences**
